title: Allow asynchronous USB microphone binding to settle
problem: Transcripted verifies AUHAL's device ID immediately after setDeviceID, so a Logitech C920 driver that publishes a successful route change asynchronously is rejected before the existing settle delay and eventually appears unavailable.
reproduce: Model a C920 route whose setDeviceID call succeeds while the immediate deviceID read remains on the prior microphone. The pinned baseline throws selectedDeviceNotBound before the settle phase.
acceptance: A successful asynchronous USB route command reaches the existing 300 ms settle phase; driver errors, zero IDs, and routes that remain stale after settling are still rejected.
repair: Validate the selected ID before binding, return a successful changed binding to the caller's settle phase, and retain strict verification on the delayed snapshot.

verification.limitations: BCL proves the source-level two-phase binding contract on the pinned baseline and candidate. A separate focused Swift harness reproduced baseline red and candidate green on macOS 15.7.2. Transcripted requires macOS 26 and full Xcode for its complete build; physical C920 capture remains unverified.
verification.ownerCheck: Install the PR build on macOS 26, select the Logitech HD Pro Webcam C920, trigger dictation repeatedly after switching from another microphone, and confirm recording starts without the switching/unavailable sequence. Also confirm disconnecting the C920 still reports it unavailable.

selection.reason: The fresh issue names the exact release, USB device, user-visible failure, and reproduction steps; no competing PR or assignee existed, and the asynchronous route boundary is deterministic without hardware.

upstream.suiteOutputIncludes: PASS: asynchronous USB binding reaches strict settled verification
